notes.text: Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 15 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 31% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 127:14 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Connor Bedard is out (shoulder injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Anton Frondell has taken his spot beside Tyler Bertuzzi and Roman Kantserov.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Cameron Crotty joined from MIN on Nov 12 and has played beside Jamie Oleksiak.

VAN.head: A slightly uphill night for the Canucks
VAN.body: Chicago has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Vancouver has home-ice advantage. The Canucks can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

CHI.head: Leaning the Blackhawks’ way
CHI.body: Chicago has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Vancouver has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Canucks can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blackhawks (6-14-2) lost 4-2 to Columbus on Thursday, and the Canucks (5-18-1) lost 5-1 to Seattle the same night. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Blackhawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.318) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .393, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Canucks (.229 on chances worth .323), mostly because they’re 3-5 in one-goal games.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), don’t block many shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (31st). Chicago has scored 2.45 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 4.05, the second most. On the other side, the Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.38 goals a game, the most in the league. The Canucks hit a lot, but the Hawks mostly don’t.

Sam Rinzel (1 G / 13 A / 14 P in 21 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Frank Nazar (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Canucks, Brock Boeser (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Elias Pettersson (#40) (6 G / 17 A / 23 P in 24 GP) is next in line.

Spencer Knight (6-11-1 / .886 SV% in 18 GS) will likely start for Chicago. Vancouver has two options in net: Leevi Meriläinen (3-10-1 / .889 SV% in 15 GS) and Nikita Tolopilo (1-0-0 / .944 SV% in 1 GS). Meriläinen has started eight of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday, so Vancouver could turn to Tolopilo to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Manny Malhotra likes to send Cotter, Chytil and Boeser out against opponents’ second lines, so watch for them against Moore, Nazar and Kane.
